rationale: The stem directly concerns legitimacy of compulsory political membership. Non-domination and non-interference are not assumed from the same answer.
The stem asks whether monopoly government is morally suspect; it directly measures political-authority legitimacy rather than a bundled liberty theory.
Emergency power is a limit-on-authority item. Agreement does not by itself establish a general anti-domination or negative-liberty position.
The stem concerns the presumption of political obedience under injustice. Tactical direct action and a general theory of liberty are separate questions.
Consent and exit are proposed as standards of political legitimacy. The answer must not mechanically force anti-domination and non-interference to co-move.

Making worker-owned firms easier to form changes the rules and ownership structure before market distribution. Under the current construct definition this is the predistribution side, not redistribution.
Making ownership more contestable changes institutional rules before distribution and therefore points toward the current construct's predistribution pole.
The stem measures permission for peaceful exchange despite planners' preferred pattern. It does not by itself establish substantive equality or a complete theory of property.
Treating persons as instruments of one imposed collective blueprint is directly an anti-domination/anti-instrumental concern.
The stem concerns plural individual ends versus an official hierarchy of goals. Property and substantive equality do not follow from the answer.

A low-paternalism safety-net design is not equivalent to redistribution-versus-predistribution, deregulation, or state-versus-exit. Deactivate until a direct benefit-design/paternalism construct exists.
Cash versus restricted in-kind aid is a transfer-design question. Deactivate rather than use it as a proxy for generic state action, deregulation, or redistribution orientation.
Freedom to form worker organizations and bargain collectively directly measures associational liberty; it does not establish a general property theory.
Meaningful exit and non-rigged background rules are conditions against domination in employment. Property legitimacy and generic non-interference are separate questions.
The stem directly concerns insulated workplace authority and contestability, so anti-domination is the primary construct.
